```{r setup}
#| code-summary: "Setup: the funded studies and the release"
source(here::here("common.R"))

# Funded studies, transcribed from the Q1 2026 Advisory Committee deck.
# `teams` links a study to its datasets in the release (the `team` column).
studies <- read_csv(here("monitor/network_studies.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(cohort = factor(cohort, c("Pilots '23", "Pilots '25", "RfP1", "RfP2")),
         label = paste0(pi, " · ", cohort),
         step = recode(cadence, annual = 1, biannual = 0.5, `15-month` = 1.25,
                       none = NA_real_))
recruiting <- studies |> filter(!is.na(age_min))

scores_all <- load_levante_latest("scores")
scores <- load_levante_clean() |> add_waves()
data_ref <- unique(scores_all$redivis_source)

study_teams <- recruiting |>
  select(label, cohort, team = teams) |>
  separate_longer_delim(team, ";") |>
  filter(team != "")
partner_teams <- setdiff(unique(scores$team), study_teams$team)

# each child in the release, with the study (or partner dataset) it belongs to
children <- scores |>
  left_join(study_teams |> select(team, label), by = "team") |>
  mutate(label = coalesce(label, paste0(site_labels_named[team], " · partner"))) |>
  group_by(label, user_id) |>
  summarise(first_age = min(age, na.rm = TRUE), waves = max(wave),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(first_age = if_else(is.finite(first_age), first_age, NA_real_))

actual <- children |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(n_children = n(),
            age_lo = quantile(first_age, .05, na.rm = TRUE),
            age_mid = median(first_age, na.rm = TRUE),
            age_hi = quantile(first_age, .95, na.rm = TRUE),
            wave2 = sum(waves >= 2), wave3 = sum(waves >= 3), .groups = "drop")

with_data <- recruiting |> semi_join(actual, by = "label")
long_with_data <- with_data |> filter(longitudinal) |>
  left_join(actual, by = "label")

cohort_pal <- c("Pilots '23" = "#4477AA", "Pilots '25" = "#EE6677",
                "RfP1" = "#228833", "RfP2" = "#CCBB44", "Partner" = "#BBBBBB")

# planned coverage: each recruited year-cohort followed by its planned waves.
# Kievit and Ngo recruit two discrete cohorts rather than an age band.
enroll_ages <- function(pi, a, b) {
  if (pi == "Rogier Kievit") c(5, 9) else if (pi == "Zoe Ngo") c(4, 6) else a:b
}
planned <- recruiting |>
  mutate(enroll_age = pmap(list(pi, age_min, age_max), enroll_ages)) |>
  unnest(enroll_age) |>
  mutate(x_end = enroll_age + if_else(n_waves <= 1 | is.na(step), 0,
                                      (n_waves - 1) * step))
planned_by_age <- planned |>
  reframe(age = seq(enroll_age, floor(x_end)), .by = c(label, enroll_age, x_end)) |>
  count(age, name = "year_cohorts")
actual_by_age <- scores |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  distinct(user_id, age = floor(age)) |>
  count(age, name = "children")
peak_planned <- planned_by_age$age[which.max(planned_by_age$year_cohorts)]
peak_actual <- actual_by_age$age[which.max(actual_by_age$children)]
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Summary

**Data:** the funded-study plans in the Q1 2026 Advisory Committee deck,
and `r data_ref` for what has been collected.

- LEVANTE has `r nrow(studies)` funded studies in four funding rounds.
  `r nrow(recruiting)` recruit children, in
  `r n_distinct(recruiting$country)` countries;
  `r sum(recruiting$longitudinal)` are longitudinal.
- `r nrow(with_data)` of them have data in the release, plus
  `r length(partner_teams)` partner datasets: `r fmt_n(n_distinct(scores$user_id))`
  children in all.
- The plans put the most coverage at age `r peak_planned`; the children in
  the release are most numerous at age `r peak_actual`.
  `r fmt_pct(mean(children$first_age < 6, na.rm = TRUE))` of children were
  under 6 at their first run.
- Of the `r nrow(long_with_data)` longitudinal studies with data,
  `r sum(long_with_data$wave2 >= 20)` have 20 or more children in a second
  wave and `r sum(long_with_data$wave3 >= 20)` in a third.
:::

# Planned and actual ages

Each row is a funded study, plus the partner datasets in the release.
Coloured squares are the ages the study plans to recruit. For studies with
data, the black line spans the middle 90% of children's ages at their first
run, and the dot marks the median.

```{r ages, fig.height=8}
#| label: fig-ages
#| fig-cap: "Planned enrollment ages (coloured squares) and, for studies with data, the middle 90% (line) and median (dot) of children's ages at their first run."
rows <- bind_rows(
  recruiting |> arrange(cohort, age_min, age_max) |> select(label, cohort),
  actual |> filter(str_ends(label, "partner")) |> transmute(label, cohort = "Partner"))
row_levels <- rev(rows$label)

planned |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, row_levels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(y = label)) +
  geom_tile(aes(x = enroll_age, fill = cohort), colour = "white",
            width = 0.92, height = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_linerange(data = actual |> mutate(label = factor(label, row_levels)),
                 aes(xmin = age_lo, xmax = age_hi), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = actual |> mutate(label = factor(label, row_levels)),
             aes(x = age_mid), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cohort_pal, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:15, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
```

# Planned and actual waves

For the longitudinal studies with data: open circles are the planned waves,
filled circles the waves reached, sized by the number of children. A child's
runs of a task count as separate waves when they are at least 90 days apart.

```{r waves, fig.height=4.5}
#| label: fig-waves
#| fig-cap: "Planned waves (open circles) and waves reached (filled, sized and labelled by the number of children), for longitudinal studies with data."
reached <- children |>
  semi_join(long_with_data, by = "label") |>
  reframe(wave = seq_len(max(waves)), n = map_int(wave, \(k) sum(waves >= k)),
          .by = label)
planned_waves <- long_with_data |>
  reframe(wave = seq_len(n_waves), .by = label)

ggplot(mapping = aes(x = wave, y = label)) +
  geom_point(data = planned_waves, shape = 1, size = 9, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = reached, aes(size = n), colour = "black") +
  geom_text(data = reached, aes(label = fmt_n(n)), nudge_x = 0.22, hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 7, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.7)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:5, expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.6))) +
  labs(x = "Wave", y = NULL)
```

# Coverage by age

Top: how many planned year-cohorts reach each age, following each recruited
year forward through its planned waves. Bottom: children in the release with
a run at each age.

```{r coverage-by-age, fig.height=5.5}
#| label: fig-coverage-by-age
#| fig-cap: "Planned year-cohorts reaching each age (top) and children in the release with a run at each age (bottom)."
p_planned <- ggplot(planned_by_age, aes(age, year_cohorts)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4477AA") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:16, limits = c(1.5, 16.5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Planned year-cohorts")
p_actual <- ggplot(actual_by_age, aes(age, children)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey40") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:16, limits = c(1.5, 16.5)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Children with a run")
patchwork::wrap_plots(p_planned, p_actual, ncol = 1)
```

# Planned coverage by study

Each line is one recruited year-cohort followed through its study's planned
waves (dots); a study's year-cohorts are stacked.

```{r planned-lines, fig.height=9}
#| label: fig-planned-lines
#| fig-cap: "Planned coverage by study: each recruited year-cohort followed through its planned waves (dots)."
site_order <- recruiting |>
  arrange(cohort, age_min, age_max) |>
  mutate(base_y = n() - row_number() + 1) |>
  select(label, base_y)

lines <- planned |>
  arrange(label, enroll_age) |>
  group_by(label) |>
  mutate(k = n(), j = row_number(),
         offset = if_else(k == 1, 0, (j - (k + 1) / 2) / (k - 1) * 0.84)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  left_join(site_order, by = "label") |>
  mutate(y = base_y + offset)
dots <- lines |>
  mutate(wv = map2(n_waves, step, \(n, s) if (is.na(n) || n <= 1 || is.na(s)) 0L else 0:(n - 1))) |>
  unnest(wv) |>
  mutate(wave_age = enroll_age + if_else(is.na(step), 0, wv * step))

ggplot() +
  geom_segment(data = lines, aes(enroll_age, y, xend = x_end, yend = y, colour = cohort),
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(data = dots, aes(wave_age, y, colour = cohort), size = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cohort_pal, name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = site_order$base_y, labels = site_order$label,
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.7)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:16, expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
```

# Notes

- **Source.** Ages are the deck's annex cards; wave schedules are its
  cohort tables. Where the two disagree the more specific value is used, and
  `monitor/network_studies.csv` records it in `notes`.
- **Planned coverage is an upper bound.** Each recruited year is followed
  forward independently, which overstates the oldest ages for studies whose
  stated age band already includes follow-up years.
- **Not longitudinal.** The three 2025 pilots for ages 2–5 (Nelson, Mariño,
  Bohn) are single visits, although the deck lists follow-up waves for them.
- **Discrete cohorts.** Kievit (about 5 and 9) and Ngo (4 and 6) recruit two
  separate age groups.
- **Linking studies to data.** The 2023 pilot listed under Bohn at Leuphana
  was collected at MPI EVA Leipzig (`pilot_mpieva_de`). The RfP1
  younger-sibling datasets (`rfp1_utdt_intl`, `rfp1_mpib_intl`) are counted
  with their studies (Calero, Ngo).

# Revision history

- **2026-10-30.** Adds what has been collected, from the pinned release:
  actual ages and waves by study, and children by age next to the planned
  coverage. The study table moves to `monitor/network_studies.csv`, with a
  column linking each study to its datasets. Previously "09 — LEVANTE
  network: enrollment ages & longitudinal coverage".
